content.text: No Customer-payable liquidated damages, penalty, or early-termination fee appears anywhere in the Agreement, and §9.4 affirmatively limits Customer's termination exposure.

input.quote: Customer owes Fees only for conforming Services provided through the effective termination date, and Vendor shall promptly refund prepaid Fees allocable to the period after that date.
input.rationale: The Agreement contains no liquidated damages, penalty, or early-termination/minimum-fee obligation payable by Customer. Searches for "liquidated damages", "penalty", "termination fee", "shortfall", and every termination and fee provision (§§ 6.2, 7.1–7.5, 9.1–9.5, 10.1–10.2, 21.1–21.4, 22.2, 27.3) return no Customer-payable liquidated amount. To the contrary, § 9.4 gives Customer a convenience-termination right under which it "owes Fees only for conforming Services provided through the effective termination date" with a refund of prepaid Fees, § 27.3 allows force-majeure termination "without penalty", and § 7.1 bars unstated minimum-use or similar charges. This meets the preferred position (Customer pays no liquidated damages or penalties), so no redline is proposed. The § 2.1 take-or-pay minimum commitment is a volume commitment rather than a liquidated damages or penalty mechanic and is addressed under the minimum-commitment rule; we do not flag it twice here. The only Customer payment triggered by a shortfall (§ 22.2 audit underpayment) is payment of amounts actually owed plus audit costs, not a liquidated sum.
